newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells Fed's Greenspan it curbs inflation.
newsitem.headline: China tells Fed's Greenspan it curbs inflation.

text.p: Chinese President Jiang Zemin told U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan that China has achieved its goal of curbing inflation, the official Xinhua news agency said on Thursday.
China had attained its goal after a three-year drive to keep prices in check, the official news agency quoted Jiang as telling the chief U.S. inflation fighter.
Jiang, who is also Communist Party chief, said the economy had maintained relatively high growth despite efforts on the inflation front.
China's economy grew 9.7 percent last year while benchmark retail price inflation was a modest 6.1 percent.
Price rises have been even lower this year and are far below the 14.8 percent reached in 1995 and the communist-era high of 21.7 percent in 1994.
Jiang also said he hoped Greenspan's visit would enhance cooperation between the financial sectors of the two countries.
Greenspan briefed Jiang on current economic and financial developments in the United States, Xinhua said.
Greenspan is in Beijing to meet China's top financial officials.
China has been eager to step up its exchanges with central banks around the world as part of an effort to strengthen its financial system.
Also present at the meeting were Dai Xianglong, governor of the People's Bank of China, or central bank, as well as vice governor Chen Yuan and U.S. ambassador to China James Sasser.
Greenspan is due to leave China on Friday to return to the United States.
